title: Rust Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: println! prints text and starts a new line. main is the program entry point.

examples.title: Keep a value
examples.description: let creates a name for a value. Values cannot be changed unless you ask for mut.

examples.title: Change a value
examples.description: mut means this binding may change. It makes the choice to change data clear.

examples.title: Pick a value with if
examples.description: if can produce a value. Both branches here return text of the same type.

examples.title: Count with a range
examples.description: 1..=3 includes both ends. A for loop visits each number in the range.

examples.title: Grow a list
examples.description: A Vec stores values in order. push adds a value at the end.

examples.title: Return a result
examples.description: The last expression can be a function result. It has no trailing semicolon.
examples.code:
fn twice(n: i32) -> i32 { n * 2 }
fn main() { println!("{}", twice(4)); }

examples.title: Move ownership
examples.description: A String owns its text. Assigning it to another variable moves that ownership.

examples.title: Read without taking ownership
examples.description: A reference borrows a value. It lets code read the value while its owner keeps it.

examples.title: Handle a missing value
examples.description: Option holds Some(value) or None. unwrap_or gives a fallback for None.

examples.title: Handle a failed action
examples.description: Result holds Ok for success or Err for failure. Parsing text can fail.

examples.title: Group named data
examples.description: A struct describes named fields. Each Book value can hold its own title.
